maya: quick heads-up — ran a small quant smoke on the new rllm-3b-v1 candidate (gptq-int8-hybrid) against sql2text-finance. seeing a surprisingly large formatting/hallucination delta specifically on the numerical-table examples.

maya: baseline (fp16) macro-acc: 86.3
maya: gptq-int8-hybrid: 78.9 (-7.4)
maya: awq-int8 (same model): 83.1 (-3.2)

liam: ouch. do you have an example? is it truncation or invented numbers?

maya: mostly invented numbers + lost trailing zeros in amounts. also bullet lists inside cells turned into inline text (markdown bullets removed). small example:

maya: ```
Input: SELECT sum(amount) FROM payments GROUP BY category;
FP16 output: "| category | total_amount |\n|---------|--------------|\n| A       | 12,340.00    |\n| B       | 3,210.50     |"
GPTQ-INT8 output: "| category | total_amount |\n|---------|--------------|\n| A       | 12,34        |\n| B       | 3210         |"
```

alex: hmm that smells like per-layer quant scale underflow + a formatting tokenization sensitivity. did you run with kv-cache enabled?

maya: yes, tests were against hosted profile with kv-cache on and batch_size=1. replicated on dedicated profile WITHOUT cache and got slightly better numbers (80.2) but still worse than fp16.

sara: can you paste the eval command and run id? I'll kick off per-layer logs.

maya: ```bash
./eval.py --model rllm-3b-v1 --quant gptq-int8 --task sql2text --dataset finance --seed 42 --run-id quantrun-1823 --cache-on 
```

maya: run id quantrun-1823 (logs at s3://redwood-ml/quant-logs/quantrun-1823)

eval-bot: evaluation finished — run=quantrun-1823; samples=2,345; macro-acc=78.9; halluc-rate=0.12; format-error-rate=0.093

liam: halluc-rate up from 0.04 baseline to 0.12? that's big. could be calibration shift in softmax from quant noise. did you try AWQ per-layer-fallback?

maya: AWQ improved halluc-rate to 0.07 but still not at fp16. we also tried GPTQ with group-size tuning (g=64 -> g=128) and saw small gains.

alex: action items:
- run per-layer activation histograms for the worst 500 examples (maya)
- try selective FP16 for final transformer block + int8 elsewhere (liam)
- run AWQ with per-layer clip heuristics and compare token-level diffs (sara)
- check tokenizer differences between compiled runtime and local eval (alex)

sara: I'll start AWQ-per-layer-clipping now, pushing debug tar to /mnt/quant-debug/quantrun-1823 in ~30m. ping me if you want live logs.

liam: I'll prototype a selective-fp fallback patch (selective-fp-lastblock) and run on dedicated infra; will post numbers later.

maya: if this narrows down to KV-cache interaction we should test both warm and cold cache. also want to verify streaming vs non-streaming outputs — streaming might drop certain trailing punctuation.

alex: good point. add streaming=false experiments to the matrix.

maya: TL;DR: large formatting/numeric halluc spike for gptq-int8-hybrid on sql2text-finance. AWQ reduces but doesn't fully close gap. coordinating per-layer debug + selective-fp experiments. thanks all :thumbsup:

sara: noted. updating the quant-triage board with run=quantrun-1823 and assignees (liam, sara, maya).

liam: ping @maya — if you can drop 50 of the worst examples into a gist I'll start investigating token-level logits diffs.

maya: done — https://gist.github.com/maya/quant-worst-50 (contains inputs, fp16/out, gptq/out, token align diffs).

eval-bot: test-cases linked in ticket Q-1823. auto-scheduled nightly bisect job if no manual fix in 48h.

alex: thanks. let's aim to have a short follow-up tomorrow after first pass on per-layer logs.

maya: sounds good — will post updates in this thread.
